text:
Alex (Customer): Hey, we're seeing weird behavior with the TypeScript SDK streaming iterator after a reconnect — chunks out of order and sometimes a blank final chunk, causing our parser to crash.
Jen (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Alex. Can you share the request id and approximate time? Also which SDK version?
Alex (Customer): request_id: req_0a9f3c, around 2026-03-14T22:12:30Z. SDK @ 1.4.2 (ts). Using SSE streaming via EventSource polyfill in Cloudflare Worker.
Maya (Eng): @Jen thanks, adding to thread. Alex — do you have a minimal repro or logs from the worker? Curious if it's the polyfill or our reconnect logic.
Alex (Customer): I can repro reliably. Steps:
1) Start a streaming chat completion with streaming: true
2) Kill the network briefly (simulate worker fetch timeout)
3) Allow reconnect in client (SDK tries to resume using last_event_id header)
Result: sometimes we get the tail of the previous stream replayed after new chunks, and once we saw an empty "\n" chunk as last yield.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): Hmm, resume behavior uses last_event_id and the server will stream from the next token. If clients don't dedupe or reassemble by event id, duplicates can happen. But empty chunk is odd.
ops-bot: deploy: staging rollout v2026.3.14-18 started by maya
Maya (Eng): @Sahil can you check whether the resume response might include a keepalive newline that our TS iterator converts into an empty string yield? I recall a bug where newline-only SSE messages were treated as data: "" events.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): I'll grep logs for req_0a9f3c. Also check kernel that marks end-of-stream vs keepalive. Could be race between connection close and resume range calculation.
Jen (Support): Alex — can you paste the exact iterator consumption code? e.g., for await (const chunk of client.stream(...)) { /* */ }
Alex (Customer): Yep:
```ts
const it = client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-alpha', messages});
for await (const part of it) {
  // parse JSON parts, push tokens
  if (!part) throw new Error('empty chunk');
}
```
I get part === '' sometimes.
Maya (Eng): That code throws on empty — maybe we should be more defensive, but we should fix root cause.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): Found server logs: 2026-03-14T22:12:30Z req_0a9f3c — connection interrupted, resume_token=tok_239, resume sent, then replayed 3 tokens, then new stream. No obvious empty payload from server. However, our SSE framing layer emits an "event:"
Note: server emitted an SSE-only keepalive as "\n" to keep proxies alive.
Maya (Eng): There's a known issue: our TS client treats any newline-split chunk as a message and runs JSON.parse on it. If the keepalive is just newline, it becomes empty string. JS JSON.parse('') throws — but parts should be filtered.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): Proposal: server already emits keepalive as a comment line ":\n" but some proxies strip leading colon. If stripped, it becomes blank data: header. On resume we might get a leftover blank event that clients see. We should either change server to send "data: \n" or make SDK ignore empty data events.
Jen (Support): Immediate mitigation for Alex: update client loop to skip falsy parts. Would that work for you temporarily?
Alex (Customer): Yes, can do that. But we still need fix — duplicates break idempotency. Our dedupe is based on token indexes in metadata but replayed tokens had overlapping indexes.
Maya (Eng): Overlapping indexes suggests resume offset calculation might be off-by-one if last_event_id rounding differs between client and server.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): I reproduced locally with our SSE proxy emulating CF worker behavior. Reconnect flow did replay 1 token sometimes when last_event_id was processed after the close event. Root cause: race where the server acknowledges last_event_id but proxies buffer trailing keepalive causing replay.
ci-bot: test: streaming-resume-regression added to flaky suite
Maya (Eng): Plan:
- Short term (patch): TS SDK should filter empty/whitespace-only events before yielding. Also add dedupe by event id in iterator (client-side).
- Mid term (server): Make keepalive a comment (": keepalive") and ensure proxies preserve it, or send structured heartbeat with event:heartbeat so clients can ignore reliably.
- Instrumentation: add tracing to resume path to log last_event_id and server resume offset.
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): I'll open a runtime PR to log resume tokens and update server keepalive format. Maya, can you add a TS SDK PR to ignore empty events and dedupe by event id? Also add unit tests simulating CF worker polyfill behavior.
Maya (Eng): On it. I'll target a patch 1.4.3 today. Adding test that simulates newline-stripping proxy and replayed token. Also include a fix: skip if chunk.trim().length === 0.
Jen (Support): Alex — once we have the SDK patch, can you try 1.4.3-rc when available and confirm? Meanwhile please add defensive skip in your parser.
Alex (Customer): Will do. Quick note — we're also seeing slight latency increase after reconnect, might be because client retries back-to-back and overloads worker. Do you want a separate ticket?
Maya (Eng): Yes please open a new thread for latency post-reconnect. This one focused on ordering/empty-chunk dupes. Assigning:
- Maya: TS SDK patch, tests
- Sahil: runtime/server resume logging and keepalive change
- Jen: customer comms and verification
Action items: create PRs, link to this thread, add e2e repro in CI.
ops-bot: deploy: staging rollout v2026.3.14-18 completed
Maya (Eng): PR #4821 opened: ts: ignore-empty-sse-chunks & dedupe by event id. Tests added. cc @jen-support
Sahil (Eng-Runtime): PR #4822 opened: runtime: explicit heartbeat event and resume-logging
Jen (Support): Thanks everyone. Alex — I'll follow up here when 1.4.3-rc is available. Let me know if you need help applying the quick local filter.
Alex (Customer): Thanks all, patch looks promising. I'll try the quick skip for now and report back.
Maya (Eng): noted for release notes: "fix: handle keepalive/empty SSE chunks, improve resume dedupe"
